c.tagline: Tiny island capital where turquoise sea meets city life.

taxi.color: white/silver sedan with rooftop TAXI sign
taxi.fareNote: Flat zone fares within Malé (~MVR 25-35 by day, higher after midnight); trips to Hulhumalé, Villingili and the airport across the Sinamalé Bridge cost more.

emergency.note: Fire: 118. Emergency dispatchers and hospital staff in Malé generally speak English.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Occasional political demonstrations near Republic Square are best given a wide berth, and remember alcohol is banned and modest dress expected on this local island.

hood_desc: The historic waterfront core of Malé with government buildings, the fish market and the main ferry jetties; central and walkable, best for first-time visitors.
A dense, mixed residential-commercial ward packed with small guesthouses and cafes, popular with budget travelers wanting an authentic local feel close to downtown.
Quieter southern residential streets near the National Stadium with local eateries and mid-range hotels, suited to business travelers and those wanting a calmer base.
A spacious, modern reclaimed island with a long sandy beach and wide streets, linked to the airport by the Sinamalé Bridge; ideal for families and travelers wanting more room to breathe.
A relaxed residential island a short ferry hop from downtown, with a laid-back local vibe that suits longer stays and budget-conscious travelers.
lodging: Hotel Jen Maldives Malé by Shangri-La

water.note: Officially treated desalinated water meets WHO standards, but most visitors' stomachs react poorly, so bottled water is safer.

transit.pay: RTL city buses are cashless only, paid via a tap card or mobile top-up app. Inter-island public ferries to Hulhumalé, Villingili and the airport are typically paid in cash (MVR) or by card at the terminal kiosk just before boarding.
transit.hours: RTL buses run roughly 6:00-24:00 at 15-30 min intervals; ferries run from about 5:00-24:00 with reduced late-night frequency; taxis operate 24/7.
transit.note: Malé itself is only about 2 sq km and almost entirely walkable; the Sinamalé Bridge lets buses and taxis drive directly to the airport island and Hulhumalé instead of relying on a boat.

bus: RTL inter-island coaches across the Sinamalé Bridge to Hulhumalé

airport.name: Velana International Airport (MLE)
airport.drive: 10 min via the Sinamalé Bridge (or a 10-min public ferry)

transit.m: RTL bus route R3 (12 min, cashless only)

tip.r: A 10% service charge is usually already added to restaurant bills; extra cash tipping is appreciated but not obligatory outside resorts.
